decisions.quote: In contrast to Javanmard and Montanari (2014), who explicitly tune a regularization parameter and model optimization constraint µ, we rely on the default configurations for all methods to better reflect how these implementations are typically used in practice.
decisions.reason: Rather than attempting to recover the exact numerical results reported by Javanmard and Montanari (2014) under their tuned hyperparameter settings, the authors went straight to alternative specifications using default parameter configurations and an additional comparator estimator, and the blind coder's cannot_be_determined establishes no error.

decisions.quote: Empirical evaluations across replications of the simulation study and the riboflavin dataset reveal a nuanced narrative regarding the practical performance of these estimators, highlighting a critical divergence between idealized settings and severely sample-starved, real-world applications. In the simulation study, multisample-splitting (Meinshausen et al., 2009) maintained strong statistical power, and the LASSO projection estimator (Zhang and Zhang, 2014) outperformed the Javanmard and Montanari (2014) method by demonstrating superior sensitivity in low-signal regimes. However, this dynamic reversed in a real high-dimensional genomic data setting.
decisions.reason: Evaluated across all re-analyses together, the alternative specifications and inclusion of the LASSO projection estimator substantively qualify the original study's conclusions by showing that multisample-splitting retains power and the LASSO projection estimator outperforms Javanmard and Montanari's method in low-signal simulation regimes, even though the original method remains superior on the empirical riboflavin dataset.

parent_objection: The first robustness judgment uses fresh Monte Carlo draws with changed default tuning. Codebook robustness axes concern re-analysis of original data, not newly simulated samples. Supplied source explicitly generates20independent realizations;the reused riboflavin dataset instead favors Javanmard/Montanari. Does any reasonable alternative analysis of the ORIGINAL dataset materially qualify the original finding? Distinguish this from new-sample simulation comparisons. Originalauthorimplementationfunctions used for newrandom draws do not by themselves establish originaldata re-analysis. Consider recordtype if needed for hybrid report,but do not change it merely because simulation appears;the substantial actualoriginal-data workflow matters. Firstquote confirms planchange,notnecessarilyrobustnesschallengeonoriginaldata.

shipped.title_o: Confidence intervals and hypothesis testing for high-dimensional regression
shipped.outcome_quote: Robustness: The results reveal a trade-off: the LASSO projection estimator performs well in low-signal settings, while Javanmard and Montanari’s method is more robust to complex correlations, improving precision and signal detection in real data.

blind_target.title: Confidence intervals and hypothesis testing for high-dimensional regression.
blind_target.evidence_quote: To evaluate the theoretical results of Javanmard and Montanari (2014), we replicate six of the original simulation scenarios (selected due to computational constraints) and the real-data application on the riboflavin (vitamin B 2 ) dataset.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: The Javanmard and Montanari method exhibited the highest precision , consistently yielding the narrowest confidence intervals and isolating signal where the Ridge and Lasso projection estimators were less sensitive. These results highlight the substantial precision gains achievable through the optimized de-biasing procedure proposed by Javanmard and Montanari (2014).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The original empirical dataset is reanalysed with alternative estimators, preserving the precision advantage of the original method. Exact recovery of original empirical numerical results is not established. Numerical discrepancies in regenerated simulations do not alone establish computational failure on original data.
